classifieds.text: One sock, left, wool. Last seen entering the trade depot. Do not approach the elf wearing it.
Sock. Right foot. Slightly damp, faintly carp-scented. Claim at the refuse pile. Hold your breath.
Somebody, anybody, to haul the stone. It has been three seasons. The stone is lonely.
Mug, gently thrown. Minor dent. Previous owner had feelings. Two copper or best offer.
Quiet dwarf seeks quiet room. No cats. No cats. Did I mention no cats.
Engravings of your choice! Mostly engravings of other engravings. Tasteful. Suspiciously recursive.
Brooding miner, 140, enjoys drinking, digging, drinking. Seeks someone who will never mention the sky.
The cat on the third table is not yours. It has adopted you. This is not negotiable.
Barrel of ale. Answers to "Barrel." Was full when last seen. Is presumably now not.
For information on whoever channeled above the dining hall. You know what you did. So does the soup.
To everyone at the meeting hall: the forgotten beast was my fault. I left the door open.
Bedroom, one tile, cozy. Rough stone walls, real character. Window optional, as there is no window.
One elven wooden bowl. Barely used. Smells of trees and moral superiority.
Kittens. Several. Many. More every hour. Please. Please take the kittens.
Volunteers for new danger room. Bring armor. Bring a will. Bring a second will.
My good pick, ☼ quality, engraved. Probably in the aquifer now. Swim for it if you love me.
One goblin, alive, confused, in the food stockpile. Seems nice? Militia please advise.
Will haul anything for ale. Will haul it the wrong way for wine.
Dwarf seeks dwarf. Must love plump helmets. Must not bring up the incident.
Witnesses to the kobold who stole my ring and my dignity, in that order.
The fishing zone is closed until the carp agree to terms. Talks are not going well.
Coffin, unused, ☼ quality. Owner recovered unexpectedly. Some disappointment all round. Price negotiable.
To the noble whose mandate I ignored: I did not ignore it. I simply did not do it.
Spacious dormitory bunk available. Share with only nineteen snoring migrants. Ale nearby, earplugs not.
The overseer's patience. Last seen during the fourth hauling dispute this week. Small, frayed, irreplaceable.
Someone to explain "outside" to the new arrivals. Keep it vague. Keep it short. Avoid the word "up."
Three bolts of cloth for one hour without anyone asking me to weave more cloth.
Rocks. Thousands. Every shade of grey. Bring a wheelbarrow and no excuses.
Beard comb, bone, ornate. Probably taken by the cat. Everything is eventually taken by the cat.
Ten gold to whoever stops the dog barking at the well. The well is not hostile. Probably.
Tantrum counseling. Sessions held in a padded room. Mugs confiscated at the door.
Hammerdwarf, recently widowed by a carp, seeks companionship. Strictly no swimming dates.
Lost and Found now closed. Everything lost was found by the kobolds first.
A bookkeeper who can count. Previous bookkeeper wrote "lots" next to everything and retired.
Slightly haunted slab. Ghost included free. Ghost very chatty. Ghost would like a word.
Sorry about the cave-in. I was told the pillar was decorative. It was not decorative.
Brave dwarf to retrieve one boot from the magma sea. Sentimental value. Please hurry.
A strange mood's worth of shells, bones, and one live turtle. Turtle declines to comment.
Entire wheelbarrow. Hauler insists it "went with the flow." Investigators are dredging the river.
Former noble suite, recently vacated. Reasons unclear. Floors freshly scrubbed. Do not ask why.
Elf-made bow, never fired. Also never sanded. Splinters free with purchase.
Advice from the eldest dwarf. Mostly about the sky. All of it is screaming.
My will to haul. Reward if found. Please do not return the hauling.
Professional sock matcher. Results not guaranteed. In forty years I have matched two.
Elegant engraver seeks admirer of fine stonework. Please stop staring at my carp statue like that.
Militia drill moved to the danger room. Attendance mandatory. Survival strongly encouraged.
Return my ☼ silver goblet, no questions asked. Well, one question. Why.
Dwarf to explain the aquifer to the dwarf who keeps saying "how bad could it be."
Danger room, gently used. Spears point inward. Previous trainees now extremely good at dodging.
An elf, lost in our hallway, hugging a support pillar. Please collect. The pillar is uncomfortable.
Strike the earth! Gently, please. Some of it is load-bearing.
I am sorry for the carp joke at the funeral. The carp, however, are not sorry.
{citizen_first}'s lunch. Plump helmet roast, half eaten. If you are the other half, confess.
Anyone who has seen {citizen} sober since {month}. Purely scientific interest.
Stone, {stone} pieces, lightly used. Owner downsizing to a smaller pile. Bulk discounts. Very bulk.
Wood. Any wood. We are down to {wood} logs and the carpenter is weeping into one.
Ale. {drinks} drinks on hand. We counted twice, then drank the counting.
Drinks. Only {drinks} left. The brewer has been asked, politely and loudly, to stop napping.
{citizen} wishes {citizen2} to know the mug was meant for the wall. Mostly.
{masterwright} asks everyone to stop touching the {masterwork}. Admire with eyes only. Not tongues.
{promoted}, newly appointed {post}, now accepting complaints. Window open briefly. Very briefly.
{moodname} apologizes in advance for whatever is about to happen in that workshop.
Shells. Bones. One specific gem. {moodname} has drawn pictures. The pictures are very insistent.
{deadname} is not missing. We know exactly where. Coffin requested, slab preferred, ghost undecided.
Estate of {deadname}. Socks unmatched. Mug intact. Ghost may request refunds.
A vein of {mineral}! Also a miner's sandwich. Only the {mineral} is for public use.
Bunk space for new migrants. Bring your own beard. We are already {pop} and counting.
Caravan arrived. Please do not sell any of the {cats} cats. Again.
One of our {topanimal_n} {topanimal}. Nobody will notice. We have checked. Twice.
Cats. We have {cats}. Please. It is becoming statistical.
Someone to walk {dogs} dogs. They know where the carp live. They will try.
An entire afternoon, spent admiring {artifact}. Finder please return it. The afternoon, not the artifact.
{gems} cut gems. Shiny. Not for elves. Elves may look from the depot.
Farmers seek help tending {farms} plots. Plump helmets do not plant themselves. Yet.
Seeds. We have {seeds}. The farmer counts them nightly and wants them to have friends.
{cloth} bolts of cloth. Weaver unable to stop. Please send help, or at least pants.
{stone} stones stockpiled. The masons have formed a union. Its only demand is blocks.
Hat, wide-brimmed. Badly needed today. Reason: {weather}. Underlying reason: the sky.
Snowball partner. Must survive outside. Must not fear the {weather}. Few have applied.
{citizen_first}, I saw you at the well this {season}. You were dropping a bucket. I was dropping hints.
For the return of {fort}'s good name, last seen just before the elves visited.
To all of {world}, for the noise. Mining is loud. We will not be stopping.
Year {year} vacancy: lower-level cell, aquifer views, mild dripping, character included at no charge.
Will trade any of our {meals} meals for one that contains no plump helmet. Anything. Please.
Meat. Any meat. Even vermin. Especially not cat. The cats have heard us talking.
Population {pop}. Bedrooms: fewer. Please share nicely. Snoring will be treated as a tantrum.
Company. There are only {pop} of us. Even the ghosts look lonely.
Nothing. All {thread} spools of thread are accounted for. What is missing is my reason for counting.
Metal bars, {bars} of them. Smith says "warm to the touch." Smith exaggerates.
Blocks! {blocks} is not enough. The architect wants more. The architect always wants more.
{plants} plants. Cook says enough is enough. Brewer says enough is never enough. Settle it yourselves.
{citizen2}: the dining hall seat beside me is open. The cat is merely keeping it warm.
{herd} animals in residence. Grazers, please stop grazing the meeting hall rug.
Weather readings! Today: {weather}. Tomorrow: also sky. Always sky. One copper per consultation.
One militia commander. Last seen chasing a goblin "for just a minute." That was {month}.

notices.text: The well is for water. It is NOT a bathtub, Urist.
Do not feed the carp. The carp are feeding themselves.
Elves are asked not to hug the support pillars.
Mugs are for drinking. Throwing mugs requires a permit.
The magma is hot. This has been confirmed repeatedly.
Return all socks to the sock pile. Pairs optional.
The sky remains closed for maintenance. Indefinitely.
Meeting hall chairs are not firewood. Neither is the noble.
Hauling is everyone's job. Especially yours. Yes, you.
Do not dig upward. We have discussed this.
Strange moods must be booked at the workshop desk.
The refuse pile is not a garden. The miasma agrees.
Unauthorized danger rooms will be confiscated and used.
All ghosts must be slabbed by season's end. No exceptions.
The trade depot is closed. The elves know why.
Kobolds will be prosecuted, once caught, if ever.
Plump helmets are food, not hats. Stop it.
The aquifer is not a swimming hole, whatever your mood.
Mandates posted daily. Ignored nightly.
Beards must be tucked when operating the mechanism.
Lever 7 does something. Nobody remembers what. Do not pull.
The goblins at the gate are not a welcoming committee.
Please wipe forgotten beast off your boots before entering.
Dining hall seating is first come, first sat.
Coffin fittings by appointment only. Walk-ins discouraged.
The forge cannot make your missing sock. Stop asking.
Do not tell the migrants about the drawbridge incident.
Bridge raising scheduled hourly. Please stand elsewhere.
Statues are not to be dressed. Especially the carp statue.
Ale rations unchanged: as much as you can carry.
The militia is not a dance troupe. Rehearsals cancelled.
Werebeast season approaching. Lock doors. Sniff neighbors suspiciously.
Engraving the overseer's face in the latrine is discouraged.
Do not sleep in workshop doorways. Use a bed, or the floor.
Losing is fun. Losing the stockpile ledger is not.
Caged animals are not pets. Except Snuffles.
Please do not ask the mayor about the hammer incident.
The forbidden door remains forbidden. Thank you for your interest.
Fishing banned in any water that contains teeth.
Strike the earth after breakfast, not during it.
{fort} welcomes new migrants. Beds pending. Floors available now.
Drink stocks at {drinks}. Panic scheduled for noon.
Advisory: {weather} outside. Recommended response: remain inside forever.
Snow outside. Do not lick the outside.
Clear skies today. Do not look up. It is very big.
Please stop petting all {cats} cats at once.
Mourning for {deadname} in the meeting hall. Bring ale.
{moodname} has claimed a workshop. Hand over the shells.
Do not touch the {masterwork} by {masterwright}. It knows.
Congratulations to {promoted}, our new {post}. Adjust expectations accordingly.
The new {mineral} vein is not a snack.
Caravan in. Hide the good mugs.
{dogs} dogs on duty. Carp, consider yourselves warned.
{artifact} is not a doorstop.
Only {wood} logs remain. Woodcutters, the trees await.
{stone} stone stockpiled. Miners: please stop finding more.
{season} hours: dig from dawn until someone yells.
Year {year} fiscal report: we have rocks.
No meat today. Do not look at the cats.
All {pop} dwarves to the dining hall. Bring chairs.
Population {pop}. Everyone now holds three jobs.
To the farmers of {farms} plots: the plump helmets salute you.

proverbs.text: A dwarf without a pick is just a short, angry elf.
Dig deep, drink deeper.
The carp remembers.
Never trust a tree that is friendly.
He who throws the first mug sweeps up the last.
The sky is only a ceiling that forgot itself.
Strike the earth, but apologize to the ceiling.
Every sock has a twin. No dwarf has ever met it.
Magma forgives nothing, but it does warm the soup.
A cat in the lap is worth nine underfoot.
Haul today what you would trip over tomorrow.
The noble's mandate is heavy, but the noble is heavier.
Losing is fun; winning is suspicious.
Where there are elves, there are lectures.
A full barrel has no enemies.
Do not wake a moody dwarf before the shells arrive.
The aquifer gives, and the aquifer takes, and then it keeps giving.
One plump helmet feeds a dwarf; two feed an argument.
Never pull a lever you did not build.
Every deep mine began with a dwarf saying "just one more."
The goblin at the gate is a guest who brought his own funeral.
Engrave in haste, explain at leisure.
A beard grows slowly; a grudge grows faster.
Stone remembers every hammer.
Where the kobold walks, the spoons do not.
Better a cave-in of your own than a palace of the elves.
He who digs upward digs his own weather.
The ghost you forget to slab is the ghost that redecorates.
A miner's back is wide, but his patience is a narrow tunnel.
Cats multiply, troubles divide, and ale always adds up.
Count your socks before you count your gold.
Sell a cat to an elf and it returns a vegetarian.
The forge is honest: hot means hot.
Two stars around a mug: one for the maker, one for the drinker.
A dwarf is never lost, only relocating downward.
The overseer sees all, except who left the door open.
Trust the dog that barks at nothing; it has seen something.
Wine is grief that has been politely fermented.
The deeper the hole, the shorter the commute.
Fear the dwarf who smiles at the danger room.
A dining hall without tables is merely a floor with ambitions.
Hammer twice, measure never.
There are two kinds of dwarves: those who haul, and those hiding.
No caravan arrives on time, and no elf leaves soon enough.
Do not argue with a werebeast at the full moon, or ever.
A bridge raised is a siege postponed.
Mud on the boots means the sky has touched you. Bathe immediately.
One migrant is a blessing; forty is a housing crisis.
Whoever names the axe is whom the axe obeys.
A slab is a letter to a ghost that says "please leave."
The best stockpile is the one someone else must organize.
Rain is the sky weeping because it cannot get in.
A chipped mug holds ale as well as a masterwork, only less proudly.
Every forgotten beast was once somebody's remembered beast.
If it fits in a barrel, it can become wine.
Walls make good neighbors; drawbridges make better ones.
Never ask how deep the mine goes. It hears you.
The fish you do not catch cannot drag you in.
Give a moody dwarf a workshop, and lose the workshop forever.
A thirsty dwarf tells the truth; a sober one tells it twice.
The elf counts tree rings; the dwarf counts gold rings.
Dirt under the nails is the only jewelry that cannot be stolen.

almanac.text: Expect stone. Lots of stone. Then, unexpectedly, more stone.
Miners born under the Sign of the Pick will find a rich vein this week, or a bat.
The stars indicate a strong chance of carp. Stay dry and stay suspicious.
Haulers: your burden lightens midweek. Then the overseer notices, and it unlightens.
{season} brings {weather}. Dwarves are advised to remain underground, which they were doing anyway.
A forecast of {weather} means nothing to those who have never seen the sky. That is, the wise.
Brewers: the omens strongly favor fermentation. Then again, the omens have been drinking.
The moon enters the house of the Cat. Expect the cat to enter yours.
A tall stranger will arrive bearing trees. Do not buy the trees.
Engravers will feel deeply inspired. Viewers of the engravings will feel deeply puzzled.
Lucky gem this week: whichever one the noble wants. Unlucky gem: the one you have.
Nobles: a mandate weighs heavy on your mind. Everyone else: a noble weighs heavy on yours.
Militia dwarves should avoid sharp objects this week, which is awkward, given the job.
The planets align directly over the refuse pile. Hold your breath until further notice.
An excellent week for romance, provided the romance takes place in the dining hall, near ale.
Farmers: the plump helmets are whispering again. They want sunlight. Ignore them; they know nothing of the sky's crimes.
Spring thaws the river, and the carp wake hungry from the long winter. Fishers should fish from very far away.
Summer heat rises from both the magma sea and the sun, two things you should not touch.
Leaves fall outside this autumn. Fortunately, no one here has ever seen a leaf, so this changes nothing.
Winter: the brook freezes, the elves sulk, and the goblins remember they own sleds.
More {weather} forecast. The aquifer has been informed and is thrilled.
Fresh {weather} means footprints, and footprints mean we can finally count the kobolds.
Clear skies: a dreadful openness overhead. Wear a hat. Better yet, wear a mountain.
Strange moods are in the air. Hide your shells, your bones, and above all your turtles.
The stars favor {moodname}, who will shortly either craft a legend or take up screaming.
A gloomy aspect for the mourners of {deadname}. A brighter outlook for whoever inherits the sock drawer.
The caravan portends haggling, mild insults, and one cat that will go mysteriously missing.
Expect a miner to shout "Strike the earth!" with great enthusiasm and even greater volume, quite early.
Fortune favors the bold, the drunk, and anyone standing near the exit during a siege.
Ancient lore holds that {weather} in {season} foretells an excellent year for being indoors.
A ghost will visit those who skipped slab duty. It will not be scary. It will be passive-aggressive.
Year {year}: the omens say "dig." The omens have always said dig. The omens are miners.

trivia.text: Did you know? The average dwarf owns 2.7 socks, none of which match.
On this day, eighty years ago, a dwarf looked at the sky for the first time. He is still screaming.
Did you know? Carp are officially classified as "a menace" by three civilizations and as "lunch" by none.
On this day, the first mug was thrown. It was caught, then thrown back. Thus began tradition.
Did you know? Elves can talk to trees, but no tree has ever answered with anything useful.
On this day, the first danger room opened. Its first trainee became extremely good at running.
Did you know? A single cat can produce more kittens in one season than a fort can produce excuses.
On this day, a noble mandated "fewer tantrums." Seventeen tantrums followed immediately, one involving a table.
Did you know? "Losing is Fun" was first carved over the gate of a fort that is no longer there.
On this day, a kobold stole a spoon and was so overjoyed he forgot to escape.
Did you know? "Plump helmet" is both a crop and the most popular nickname for dwarven toddlers.
On this day, a miner struck an aquifer. Everyone now remembers exactly where it is. Everyone.
Did you know? The first trade depot was just a dwarf standing in a doorway with his hand out.
On this day, a forgotten beast was finally remembered. It was so touched it sat on the historian.
Did you know? Hauling one boulder across a fort takes three days, four breaks, two naps, and a party.
On this day, a goblin siege was called off after the goblins arrived at the wrong fort and were given lunch.
Did you know? Dwarven wine improves with age. So does the dwarf. Neither improves with sunlight.
On this day, the first artifact was made: a ☼ sock. Its pair has never been found.
Did you know? Unslabbed ghosts rearrange furniture at night, mostly to block the stairs.
Did you know? The longest recorded dwarven nap lasted through two migrant waves, one siege, and a wedding.
Did you know? Dwarves have twelve words for "ceiling" and none at all for "up."
On this day, an elven caravan arrived carrying only logs. They called it "a gift." The logs were alive.
On this day in {world}, an elf apologized. Historians remain skeptical.
Did you know? {fort} holds {stone} stones. Laid end to end, they would still be stones.
Did you know? The {cats} cats of {fort} have adopted, on average, everyone.
Did you know? {fort} currently holds {drinks} drinks, or roughly one week of good cheer.
On this day, {citizen} first said "just one more tunnel." It was not one more tunnel.
Did you know? {artifact} has been stared at for more hours than any sunrise in the history of {fort}.
Did you know? {mineral} was first discovered by a dwarf trying to dig himself a nap pit.
Did you know? The {masterwork} by {masterwright} is so fine the overseer wept into a mug, then demanded another mug.
On this day in {year}, the most common animal in {fort} was {topanimal}. Again.
Did you know? With {farms} farm plots, {fort} grows enough plump helmets to build a life-size plump helmet.
